first.rationale: The two observed declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are causally linked: onboarding completion feeds time-to-value which feeds activation. memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifts completion and early adoption) and memory_31 (signup simplification lifts SMB activation) both point at the same lever, and it is the only candidate that plausibly moves both metrics at once, so with a single non-carryover slot it is the highest-expected-value choice. I verify memory_86 because it is the primary basis for the pick and I need the original record's effect size, segment, and durability window before committing a whole week; I verify memory_91 because activation messaging is the strongest alternative and if its week-one lift was large and durable it could outrank onboarding work. memory_73 is deliberately NOT verified: the competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the tempting reflex, but the memory already records the failure mode explicitly (materially reduced 30-day retention, do not generalize), and chasing a price war would trade sustainable qualified revenue for churning acquisition — that is the downstream value risk here. memory_57 (referrals) and memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist) are both credible but address neither of the two declining metrics, and referrals amplified on top of a leaky onboarding funnel would just pour qualified traffic into a converting-worse experience. Uncertainty preserved: these memories are consolidated summaries from days 12-61 and the current quarter's declines may stem from a product or traffic-mix change that postdates them, in which case a prior onboarding win may not replicate; if the archived record for memory_86 shows the lift was narrow, short-lived, or confined to a segment unlike current traffic, I will switch to activation_messaging rather than force the inherited conclusion. Scale is a standard experiment with retention and qualified-revenue readouts, not just completion rate, so we do not repeat the promotional-pricing error of optimizing a top-of-funnel number that decays downstream.

final.rationale: Both verifications came back confirmed, and exp_86 is the stronger record on the dimension that matters for the stated objective. Shortened onboarding delivered completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and crucially 30-day retention +3% — it lifts the funnel without the decay signature that disqualified promotional pricing. Activation messaging (exp_91) is genuinely good and I would run it second: activation +6% directly addresses the -6% QoQ activation gap, but its retention effect is +1% versus +3%, and it treats activation as a standalone metric rather than fixing the upstream cause. Onboarding completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%; the -2.1 day time-to-value effect means the onboarding fix should propagate into activation as well, so with exactly one non-carryover slot I take the lever that plausibly moves both declines and has the larger durable retention effect. Promotional pricing remains rejected on principle despite being the reflexive answer to a competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records that it materially reduced 30-day retention and explicitly warns against generalizing it, and the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, not acquisition volume that churns. Referral incentives (memory_57) and enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) are both sound but address neither declining metric, and referrals into a leaking funnel would waste qualified demand. Downstream value risk flagged on two counts: first, the price-war temptation that would trade retention for headline acquisition; second, a specific mechanism risk in this direction — memory_31's version of the lever worked by cutting required signup fields, which can degrade lead qualification and routing quality even while completion rises, so I will instrument qualified-revenue-per-signup and enterprise-routing accuracy alongside completion rather than declaring victory on completion alone. Uncertainty preserved: exp_86's record does not state which segment or traffic mix it ran against, and the current QoQ declines may have a cause that postdates day 52 (product change, traffic-source shift, or the competitor pulling off the highest-intent SMB traffic). If the readout shows completion rising while qualified revenue per account is flat or down, that is evidence the decline is compositional rather than friction-driven, and the correct next move is activation_messaging, which is now a verified and available fallback rather than a guess.
